chunks: From him, from Musa ibn 'Umar, from al-Hasan ibn Fadhl, from Ibn Bukayr and Thalathah, from Burayd, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
"The forehead is [defined as extending] to the nose; whichever of those parts touches the ground during prostration suffices [for validity], but prostrating with the entire [forehead] is superior."

key_terms.أَجْزَأَكَ: It suffices for you, indicating validity of the ritual act
key_terms.أَفْضَلُ: Superior or more virtuous, indicating recommended excellence
key_terms.إِلَى الْأَنْفِ: To the nose, defining the lower boundary of the forehead
key_terms.السُّجُودُ: Prostration, a ritual act in Islamic prayer
key_terms.الْجَبْهَةُ: The forehead, the area of the body required to touch the ground during prostration

ai.seo_question: What part of the forehead must touch the ground during Islamic prayer prostration?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the fiqh of the forehead's boundaries during sujood, establishing that contact with any part of the area extending to the nose is sufficient for validity, though full contact is preferred. This ruling addresses the practical concerns of worshippers regarding the placement of the forehead on the turbah, ensuring the ritual's validity while encouraging the ideal form of prostration as a sign of humility. It reflects the Shia emphasis on both the legal minimum (kafi) and the spiritual excellence (afdhal) in acts of worship.
